4535.text:
$Match the following and choose the correct code.
MaterialApplication
(A)Silicones(i)As a catalyst
(ii)Greases
(B)Zeolites(iii)In surgical implants
(iv)As ion exchangers
$
4535.sol:
Greases i.e. lubricant are generally prepared from silicones. Silicone greases are generally thickened with silica. It is silicone oil based with inert filters silicones is a polymer that includes silicon in its monomeric molecule. Silicon implants are inert and resist tissue in growth instead they become surrounded by a fibrous capsule. Zeolites are extremely useful as a catalyst for several important reactions involving organic molecule. e.g. ZSM-5. Ion exchanger is used extensively in small water system. Zeolite exchanger one ion from the water being treated for another ion that is in the resin.
Hence, (A) Silicones \rightarrow (ii) Greases and (iii) In surgical implants.
(B) Zeolites \rightarrow (i) Catalyst (iv) As ion exchanger i.e. correct order is (A-ii), (A-iii), (B-i), (B-iv).

$\begin{aligned}

& \therefore 2 x^3+x^2-5=(A x+B)\left(2 x^2+5\right) \\
& +(C x+1)\left(x^2-5\right) \\
& \Rightarrow 2 x^3+x^2-5=A x^3+5 A x+B x^2+5 B \\
& +C x^3-5 C x+x^2-5 \\
& \Rightarrow 2 x^3+x^2-5=x^3(A+C)+x^2(B+1) \\
& +x(5 A-5 C)+5 B-5
\end{aligned}$
On equating the coefficients of $x^3, x^2, x$ and constant, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& A+C=2, B+1=1,5 A-5 C=0 \\
& \text{and } \\
& 5 B-5=-5 \\
& B+1=1 \Rightarrow B=0 \\
& 5 A-5 C=0 \Rightarrow A=C \\
& A+C=2 \Rightarrow C+C=2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 2 C=2 \Rightarrow C=1
\end{aligned}$
Now,
and

Let

$log\left(- {x}^{2} - x + 1\right)$ is defined for 

$- {x}^{2} - x + 1 > 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + x - 1 < 0$

$⇒ \left(x - \left(\dfrac{- 1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\right)\right)\left(x - \left(\dfrac{- 1 - \sqrt{5}}{2}\right)\right) < 0$

And,

${$\left|x\right|$}^{2} - 2 $\left|x\right|$ - 8 \ge 0$

Put \left|x\right| = t$

$⇒ t \in ( - \infty , - 2 ] ∪ [ 4, \infty )$

$⇒ \left|x\right| \in ( - \infty , - 2 ] ∪ [ 4, \infty )$

But $\left|x\right|$ \ge 0 ∀ x \in R$, so

12023.text: When the axes are rotated through an angle $45 °$, the new coordinates of a point $P$ are $( 1, - 1 )$. The coordinates of $P$ in the original system are
12023.sol:
When axes are rotated through an angle $\theta$, then coordinates are

$X = xcos\theta - ysin\theta$

$= cos{45}^{∘} + sin{45}^{∘}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = \sqrt{2}$

$Y = xsin\theta + ycos\theta$

$= sin{45}^{∘} - cos{45}^{∘}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} = 0$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ in the original system are $( \sqrt{2}, 0 )$

14692.text:
Find the angular speed of rotation of the Earth, so that the apparent $g$ at the equator becomes (1/6)th of its original value.

$\left(R=6.4 $\times$10^6 \mathrm{~m}$\right)
14692.sol:
The apparent $g^{\prime}$ due to rotation of earth is given by
$g^{\prime}=g_0-\omega^2 R\begin{array}{rlrl}\Rightarrow & \frac{g_0}{6} & =g_0-\omega^2 R \quad\left(\because g^{\prime}=\frac{1}{6} g\right) \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{5}{6} g_0 & =\omega^2 R \\ \Rightarrow \quad \omega & =\sqrt{\frac{5 g_0}{6 R}} \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{5 \times 9.8}{6 \times 6400000}} \quad\left(\because g_0=9.8 \mathrm{ ms}^{-2}\right) \\ & =1.13498 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{rads}^{-1} \\ \Rightarrow & \quad \omega & \approx 1.14 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{rads}^{-1}\end{array}$

14818.text: A vessel has $6g$ of oxygen at pressure $P$ and temperature $400K$. A small hole is made in it so that oxygen leaks out. How much oxygen leaks out if the final pressure is $\dfrac{P}{2}$ and temperature is $300K$?
14818.sol:
From ideal gas equation, $PV = nRT$

$⇒ PV = \dfrac{m}{M}RT$

$⇒ P ∝ mT$

$⇒ m ∝ \dfrac{P}{T}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m2}{m1} = \dfrac{P2}{P1} \times \dfrac{T1}{T2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m2}{m1} = \dfrac{P}{2P} \times \dfrac{400}{300}$

$⇒ \dfrac{m2}{m1} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Final mass, $⇒ {m}_{2} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times {m}_{1} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 6$

$⇒ {m}_{2} = 4g$

Leaked out mass $= 6 - 4 = 2g$

19665.subject: Chemistry
19665.text:
Two statements, one Assertion (A) and the other Reason (R) are given. Choose the correct option.
Assertion: 2-aminoethanoic acid and p-aminobenzene sulphonic acid can exist as Zwitter ions while p-aminobenzoic acid cannot.
Reason: When the acid group is a relatively strong proton donor and the $-\mathrm{NH}_2$ group is sufficiently basic it can accept a $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ ion from the acid group to form the dipolar ion.
options: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is wrong but R is correct.
19665.sol:
A Zwitter ion is formed when an acidic group (proton donor) and a basic group (proton acceptor) are present in the same molecule, allowing for internal proton transfer. 2-aminoethanoic acid (glycine) contains a carboxylic acid group ($-COOH$) and an amino group ($-NH_2$), which allows it to exist as $H_3N^{+}-CH_2-COO^{-}$.

p-aminobenzene sulphonic acid (sulphanilic acid) contains a strongly acidic sulphonic acid group ($-SO_3H$) and a basic amino group ($-NH_2$), which allows it to exist as a Zwitter ion $H_3N^{+}-C_6H_4-SO_3^{-}$.

p-aminobenzoic acid contains a carboxylic acid group ($-COOH$) and an amino group ($-NH_2$). However, the basicity of the amino group attached to the benzene ring is significantly reduced due to resonance with the aromatic ring. Consequently, it is not basic enough to accept a proton from the carboxylic acid group to form a stable Zwitter ion in aqueous solution.

The Reason (R) correctly explains the requirement for Zwitter ion formation: the acid group must be a strong enough proton donor and the amino group must be sufficiently basic to accept the proton. Since the Assertion (A) correctly identifies the compounds that can form Zwitter ions and the Reason (R) provides the correct chemical principle, both are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.

Answer: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.

21694.subject: Mathematics
21694.text: The minimum value of $Z=3 x+5 y$, given subject to the constraints $x+y \geq 2, x+3 y \geq 3, x, y \geq 0$ is
21694.sol:
The objective function is $Z = 3x + 5y$.

The constraints are $x + y \geq 2$, $x + 3y \geq 3$, $x \geq 0$, and $y \geq 0$.

To find the feasible region, determine the intersection points of the boundary lines:
1. $x + y = 2$ passes through $(2,0)$ and $(0,2)$.
2. $x + 3y = 3$ passes through $(3,0)$ and $(0,1)$.

The intersection of $x + y = 2$ and $x + 3y = 3$ is found by subtracting the equations:
$(x + 3y) - (x + y) = 3 - 2 \Rightarrow 2y = 1 \Rightarrow y = 0.5$.
Substituting $y = 0.5$ into $x + y = 2$, we get $x = 1.5$.
The intersection point is $(1.5, 0.5)$.

The vertices of the unbounded feasible region are $(3,0)$, $(1.5, 0.5)$, and $(0,2)$.

Evaluate $Z = 3x + 5y$ at these vertices:
At $(3,0)$: $Z = 3(3) + 5(0) = 9$.
At $(1.5, 0.5)$: $Z = 3(1.5) + 5(0.5) = 4.5 + 2.5 = 7$.
At $(0,2)$: $Z = 3(0) + 5(2) = 10$.

Comparing the values, the minimum value of $Z$ is 7.

Answer: 7

22844.subject: Physics
22844.text: The electric flux from cube of side $1 \mathrm{ m}$ is '$\Phi$' When the side of the cube is made $3 \mathrm{ m}$ and the charge enclosed by the cube is made one third of the original value, then the flux from the bigger cube will be :
22844.sol:
According to Gauss Law, the electric flux $\Phi$ through a closed surface is given by $\Phi = \dfrac{q_{enclosed}}{\epsilon_0}$, where $q_{enclosed}$ is the total charge enclosed by the surface.

The initial flux is $\Phi = \dfrac{q}{\epsilon_0}$, where $q$ is the initial charge enclosed.

When the side of the cube is changed to $3 \text{ m}$, the size of the cube does not affect the total flux, as flux depends only on the enclosed charge.

The new charge enclosed is $q' = \dfrac{q}{3}$.

The new flux $\Phi'$ is given by $\Phi' = \dfrac{q'}{\epsilon_0} = \dfrac{q/3}{\epsilon_0} = \dfrac{1}{3} \left( \dfrac{q}{\epsilon_0} \right) = \dfrac{\Phi}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\Phi}{3}$

$[X] = [M^1 L^2 T^{-2}]$

The dimensions $[M L^2 T^{-2}]$ correspond to Energy.

If slope of tangents to hyperbola $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ is $m$,

$y=m x \pm \sqrt{a^{2} m^{2}-b^{2}} \quad$ with the points of contact

$\therefore$ Slope of tangent $=2 \therefore$ Points of contact are $\left(\frac{\pm 9 \times 2}{\sqrt{9 \times 4-4}}, \frac{\pm 4}{\sqrt{9 \times 4-4}}\right)$

26142.subject: Physics
26142.text:
List-I contains four conducting loops lying in the $XY$ plane, as shown in the figures. The loops are rotating about $Z$ axis passing through the point $O$ with time period $T$ in clockwise direction. The region $x > 0$ contains a uniform magnetic field $B$ in the $+z$ direction. List-II contains the qualitative variation of the induced current $i(t)$ for each of these loops. Choose the option which describes the correct match between the entries in List-I to those in List-II.
List-IList-II
(P) (1)
(Q) (2)
(R) (3)
(S) (4)
(5)
26142.sol:
Let us analyze the induced current $i(t)$ for each loop as it rotates clockwise with time period $T$. The magnetic field $B$ is uniform in the $+z$ direction for $x > 0$. The angular velocity is $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$. The induced EMF is $\varepsilon = -\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt} = -B \dfrac{dA}{dt}$, where $A(t)$ is the area of the loop in the region $x > 0$. The current $i(t)$ is proportional to $\dfrac{dA}{dt}$.

Loop (P):
This is a semicircle in the region $x < 0$ at $t = 0$. As it rotates clockwise, the top half of the straight edge enters the region $x > 0$. The area in $x > 0$ is a sector of angle $\theta = \omega t$.
For $0 \le t \le T/2$, the area $A(t) = \dfrac{1}{2}R^2\omega t$ increases linearly, so $\dfrac{dA}{dt}$ is a positive constant. Thus, $i(t)$ is a positive constant.
For $T/2 \le t \le T$, the loop exits the region $x > 0$, and the area decreases linearly, so $\dfrac{dA}{dt}$ is a negative constant. Thus, $i(t)$ is a negative constant.
This matches graph (3). So, P $\rightarrow$ 3.

Loop (R):
This is a single sector of angle $60^{\circ} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
For $0 \le t \le T/6$, the sector enters $x > 0$. The area increases linearly, so $i(t)$ is a positive constant.
For $T/6 \le t \le T/2$, the sector is fully inside $x > 0$. The area is constant, so $i(t) = 0$.
For $T/2 \le t \le 2T/3$, the sector exits $x > 0$. The area decreases linearly, so $i(t)$ is a negative constant.
For $2T/3 \le t \le T$, the sector is fully outside $x > 0$. The area is zero, so $i(t) = 0$.
This matches graph (1). So, R $\rightarrow$ 1.

Loop (S):
This loop consists of two identical sectors arranged symmetrically but connected such that they form a figure-8 loop (crossing at the origin). The two lobes of a figure-8 loop have opposite area vectors. As the loop rotates, the rate of change of flux in the top lobe is exactly canceled by the rate of change of flux in the bottom lobe due to their symmetric entry and exit combined with the opposite sense of traversal. Therefore, the net induced EMF and current are zero at all times.
This matches graph (4). So, S $\rightarrow$ 4.

Loop (Q):
By elimination and matching the remaining options, Q corresponds to graph (2). The loop has multiple sectors that enter and exit the magnetic field at different intervals, creating alternating positive and negative pulses of current.
So, Q $\rightarrow$ 2.

The correct matching is P $\rightarrow$ 3, Q $\rightarrow$ 2, R $\rightarrow$ 1, S $\rightarrow$ 4.

26543.text: A plano-convex lens is made of a material of refractive index n. When a small object is placed 30 cm away in front of the curved surface of the lens, an image of double the size of the object is produced. Due to reflection from the convex surface of the lens, another faint image is observed at a distance of 10 cm away from the lens. Which of the following statement(s) is (are) true?
options: The refractive index of the lens is 2.5
The radius of curvature of the convex surface is 45 cm
The faint image is erect and real
The focal length of the lens is 20 cm.
26543.sol:
$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$\dfrac{1}{60} - \dfrac{1}{\left(- 30\right)} = \dfrac{1}{f} ⇒ f = 20cm$ ...(i)
Also $\dfrac{1}{f} = \left(n - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right) = \dfrac{\left(n - 1\right)}{R}$ ....(ii)
For reflection from convex mirror (curved surface)

$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{2}{R}$ ....(iii)
R = 30 cm
From (i), (ii) and (iii)
$n = 2.5,$
Faint image erect and virtual

26710.subject: Physics
26710.text: In a new system of units, the units of mass, length, time and current are $5$ kg, $5$ m, $5$ s and $5$ A, respectively. If $\mu_0$ and $\epsilon_0$ are the permeability and permittivity of free space, respectively, then in this new system of units, the magnitude of one SI unit of $\sqrt{\mu_0/\epsilon_0}$, is:
26710.sol:
The dimensional formula for permeability of free space $\mu_0$ is $[M L T^{-2} A^{-2}]$.

The dimensional formula for permittivity of free space $\epsilon_0$ is $[M^{-1} L^{-3} T^4 A^2]$.

The dimensional formula for $\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_0}{\epsilon_0}}$ is:
$\left( \dfrac{[M L T^{-2} A^{-2}]}{[M^{-1} L^{-3} T^4 A^2]} \right)^{1/2} = \left( [M^2 L^4 T^{-6} A^{-4}] \right)^{1/2} = [M L^2 T^{-3} A^{-2}]$

Let the magnitude of $1$ SI unit in the new system be $n$. Using the principle of dimensional homogeneity:
$n_1 u_1 = n_2 u_2$
$1 \times [M_1 L_1^2 T_1^{-3} A_1^{-2}] = n \times [M_2 L_2^2 T_2^{-3} A_2^{-2}]$

Given the new units are $M_2 = 5$ kg, $L_2 = 5$ m, $T_2 = 5$ s, and $A_2 = 5$ A, while the SI units are $M_1 = 1$ kg, $L_1 = 1$ m, $T_1 = 1$ s, and $A_1 = 1$ A.

$n = \left( \dfrac{M_1}{M_2} \right) \left( \dfrac{L_1}{L_2} \right)^2 \left( \dfrac{T_1}{T_2} \right)^{-3} \left( \dfrac{A_1}{A_2} \right)^{-2}$

$n = \left( \dfrac{1}{5} \right) \left( \dfrac{1}{5} \right)^2 \left( \dfrac{1}{5} \right)^{-3} \left( \dfrac{1}{5} \right)^{-2}$

$n = 5^{-1} \times 5^{-2} \times 5^3 \times 5^2$

$n = 5^{-1 - 2 + 3 + 2} = 5^2 = 25$

Thus, the magnitude of one SI unit in the new system of units is $25$.

Answer: $25$

27246.text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I: Aniline reacts with con. ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ followed by heating at $453 - 473K$ gives p-aminobenzene sulphonic acid, which gives blood red colour in the 'Lassaigne's test'.

Statement II: In Friedel - Craft's alkylation and acylation reactions, aniline forms salt with the ${AlCl}_{3}$ catalyst. Due to this, nitrogen of aniline acquires a positive charge and acts as deactivating group.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is false but statement II is true
Both statement I and statement II are false
Statement I is true but statement II is false
Both statement I and statement II are true
27246.sol:
Aniline reacts with $conc . {H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$followed by heating at $453 - 473K$gives p-aminobenzene sulphonic acid, which gives blood red colour in the 'Lassaigne's test'Nitrogen, sulphur, and halogens present in organic compounds are detected by Lassaigne's test. Here, a small piece of Na metal is heated in a fusion tube with the organic compound. The principle is that, in doing so, Na converts all the elements present into ionic form.

Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction (alkylation and acetylation) due to salt formation with aluminium chloride, the Lewis acid, which is used as a catalyst. Due to this, nitrogen of aniline acquires positive charge and hence acts as a strong deactivating group for further reaction.

28649.subject: Chemistry
28649.text:
Number of paramagnetic complexes among the following is ________.
$[\text{MnBr}_4]^{2-}$, $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$, $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$, $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$, $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$, $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$, $[\text{Ti(CN)}_6]^{3-}$, $[\text{Cu(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$, $[\text{Co(C}_2\text{O}_4\text{)}_3]^{3-}$
28649.sol:
To determine the magnetic nature of the given complexes, we analyze the oxidation state, electronic configuration, and the nature of the ligands for each central metal atom/ion:

1. $[\text{MnBr}_4]^{2-}$: Mn$^{2+}$ has a $3d^5$ configuration. Br$^-$ is a weak field ligand. The complex is tetrahedral with $5$ unpaired electrons. (Paramagnetic)

2. $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$: Ni$^{2+}$ has a $3d^8$ configuration. Cl$^-$ is a weak field ligand. The complex is tetrahedral with $2$ unpaired electrons. (Paramagnetic)

3. $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$: Ni$^{2+}$ has a $3d^8$ configuration. CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand. The complex is square planar ($dsp^2$) with all electrons paired. (Diamagnetic)

4. $[\text{Ni(CO)}_4]$: Ni$^0$ has a $3d^8 4s^2$ configuration, which becomes $3d^{10}$ in the presence of the strong field ligand CO. The complex is tetrahedral with all electrons paired. (Diamagnetic)

5. $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$: Co$^{3+}$ has a $3d^6$ configuration. F$^-$ is a weak field ligand. The complex is octahedral and high spin ($t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$) with $4$ unpaired electrons. (Paramagnetic)

6. $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$: Fe$^{2+}$ has a $3d^6$ configuration. CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand. The complex is octahedral and low spin ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$) with all electrons paired. (Diamagnetic)

7. $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$: Mn$^{3+}$ has a $3d^4$ configuration. CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand. The complex is octahedral and low spin ($t_{2g}^4 e_g^0$) with $2$ unpaired electrons. (Paramagnetic)

8. $[\text{Ti(CN)}_6]^{3-}$: Ti$^{3+}$ has a $3d^1$ configuration. The complex is octahedral ($t_{2g}^1 e_g^0$) with $1$ unpaired electron. (Paramagnetic)

9. $[\text{Cu(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$: Cu$^{2+}$ has a $3d^9$ configuration. The complex is octahedral ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^3$) with $1$ unpaired electron. (Paramagnetic)

10. $[\text{Co(C}_2\text{O}_4\text{)}_3]^{3-}$: Co$^{3+}$ has a $3d^6$ configuration. Oxalate ($\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$) acts as a strong field ligand for Co$^{3+}$. The complex is octahedral and low spin ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$) with all electrons paired. (Diamagnetic)

Therefore, the paramagnetic complexes are $[\text{MnBr}_4]^{2-}$, $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$, $[\text{Mn(CN)}_6]^{3-}$, $[\text{Ti(CN)}_6]^{3-}$, and $[\text{Cu(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$.

The total number of paramagnetic complexes is $6$.

Answer: $6$

Molar mass of $\mathrm{Cu}=63.54 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
Molar mass of $\mathrm{O}_{2}=32 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
Faraday Constant $=96500 \mathrm{C} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$
Molar volume at $\mathrm{STP}=22.4 \mathrm{~L}$]

Eq of Cu = Eq of $O_2$
$\dfrac{300 \times 10^{-3} \times 2}{63.54} = n_{O_2} \times 4$
$2.36 \times 10^{-3} = n_{O_2}$
When current is further passed

$n_{O_2} = 2.611 \times 10^{-3}$
Total $O_2$ released
$= [10^{-3} \times (2.36 + 2.611)] \times 22400$ ml
$= 111.35$ ml

32542.text: A cup of water at $5^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ (system) is placed in a microwave oven and the oven is turned on for one minute during which the water begins to boil. Which of the following option is true ?
32542.sol:
For water heating in a microwave:
Heat (q): The microwave radiates electromagnetic energy that is absorbed by water molecules, so q = +ve
Work (w): As water heats and boils, it expands against atmospheric pressure. The system does work on the surroundings, so w = -ve
Internal Energy (ΔU): From the first law, ΔU = q + w. Since heat absorbed (+ve) is much larger in magnitude than work done against atmosphere (-ve), the net change is ΔU = +ve (confirmed by temperature increase from 5°C to boiling)
Therefore: q = +ve, w = -ve, ΔU = +ve

34784.text: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $xdy = \left(y + {x}^{3}cosx\right)dx$ with $y\left(\pi\right) = 0,$ then $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is equal to:

$⇒ \dfrac{xdy - ydx}{{x}^{2}} = \dfrac{{x}^{3}cosxdx}{{x}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = ∫ xcosxdx$

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{x} = xsinx - ∫ 1 . sinxdx$

Therefore, $\dfrac{y}{x} = xsinx + cosx + C$

At $x = \pi, y = 0,$

$0 = - 1 + C$

$⇒ C = 1, x = \pi, y = 0$

So, $\dfrac{y}{x} = xsinx + cosx + 1$

$⇒ y = {x}^{2}sinx + xcosx + x$

Hence, $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{2} .$

35092.text: Let $f:(1,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function defined as $f(x) = \dfrac{x-1}{x+1}$. Let $f^{i+1}(x) = f(f^i(x))$, $i=1, 2, \ldots, 25$, where $f^1(x)=f(x)$. If $g(x) + f^{26}(x) = 0$, $x \in (1, \infty)$, then the area of the region bounded by the curves $y=g(x)$, $2y=2x-3$, $y=0$ and $x=4$ is:
35092.sol:
Given $f(x) = \dfrac{x-1}{x+1}$. Let us find the first few compositions of $f(x)$:

$f^2(x) = f(f(x)) = \dfrac{\dfrac{x-1}{x+1}-1}{\dfrac{x-1}{x+1}+1} = \dfrac{x-1-x-1}{x-1+x+1} = \dfrac{-2}{2x} = -\dfrac{1}{x}$

$f^3(x) = f(f^2(x)) = f\left(-\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = \dfrac{-\dfrac{1}{x}-1}{-\dfrac{1}{x}+1} = \dfrac{-1-x}{-1+x} = \dfrac{x+1}{1-x}$

$f^4(x) = f(f^3(x)) = f\left(\dfrac{x+1}{1-x}\right) = \dfrac{\dfrac{x+1}{1-x}-1}{\dfrac{x+1}{1-x}+1} = \dfrac{x+1-1+x}{x+1+1-x} = \dfrac{2x}{2} = x$

Since $f^4(x) = x$, the sequence of functions is periodic with a period of $4$.

Therefore, $f^{26}(x) = f^{4 \times 6 + 2}(x) = f^2(x) = -\dfrac{1}{x}$.

We are given $g(x) + f^{26}(x) = 0$, which implies:
$g(x) - \dfrac{1}{x} = 0 \Rightarrow g(x) = \dfrac{1}{x}$

We need to find the area of the region bounded by the curves $y = \dfrac{1}{x}$, $y = x - \dfrac{3}{2}$ (from $2y = 2x - 3$), $y = 0$, and $x = 4$.

First, find the point of intersection of $y = \dfrac{1}{x}$ and $y = x - \dfrac{3}{2}$:
$\dfrac{1}{x} = x - \dfrac{3}{2} \Rightarrow 2x^2 - 3x - 2 = 0$
$(2x+1)(x-2) = 0$
Since $x \in (1, \infty)$, we get $x = 2$.

The line $y = x - \dfrac{3}{2}$ intersects the x-axis ($y = 0$) at $x = \dfrac{3}{2}$.

The required area $A$ is bounded by $y = x - \dfrac{3}{2}$ from $x = \dfrac{3}{2}$ to $x = 2$, and by $y = \dfrac{1}{x}$ from $x = 2$ to $x = 4$.

$A = \int_{3/2}^{2} \left(x - \dfrac{3}{2}\right) dx + \int_{2}^{4} \dfrac{1}{x} dx$

Evaluating the first integral:
$\int_{3/2}^{2} \left(x - \dfrac{3}{2}\right) dx = \left[ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(x - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2 \right]_{3/2}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(2 - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2 - 0 = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{8}$

Evaluating the second integral:
$\int_{2}^{4} \dfrac{1}{x} dx = [\log_e x]_{2}^{4} = \log_e 4 - \log_e 2 = \log_e 2$

Total Area = $\dfrac{1}{8} + \log_e 2$

35676.text: Let $[\cdot]$ denote the greatest integer function and $f(x)=\lim _{\mathrm{n} \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{\mathrm{n}^{3}} \sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{\mathrm{n}}\left[\frac{\mathrm{k}^{2}}{3^{x}}\right]$. Then $12 \sum_{\mathrm{j}=1}^{\infty} f(\mathrm{j})$ is equal to $\_\_\_\_$.
35676.sol:
Let [·] denote the greatest integer function. We have $f(x) = \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n^3} \sum_{k=1}^n [\frac{k^2}{3^x}]$.
For large $n$: $\sum_{k=1}^n [\frac{k^2}{3^x}] \approx \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{k^2}{3^x} = \frac{1}{3^x} \cdot \frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} \approx \frac{n^3}{3 \cdot 3^x}$
Therefore: $f(x) = \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{n^3} \cdot \frac{n^3}{3 \cdot 3^x} = \frac{1}{3^{x+1}}$
Computing the infinite series:
$\sum_{j=1}^\infty f(j) = \sum_{j=1}^\infty \frac{1}{3^{j+1}} = \frac{1}{3^2} + \frac{1}{3^3} + \frac{1}{3^4} + \cdots$
$= \frac{1}{9} \cdot (1 + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{9} + \cdots) = \frac{1}{9} \cdot \frac{1}{1 - 1/3} = \frac{1}{9} \cdot \frac{3}{2} = \frac{1}{6}$
Therefore: $12 \sum_{j=1}^\infty f(j) = 12 \cdot \frac{1}{6} = 2$

Let the threshold frequency be ${\lambda}_{0}$.

By the equation of photoelectric effect, for wavelength $\lambda$,

$e{V}_{0} = hc\left(\dfrac{1}{\lambda} - \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{0}}\right) . . . ( i )$

For the wavelength $2\lambda$,

$\dfrac{e{V}_{0}}{4} = hc\left(\dfrac{1}{2\lambda} - \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{0}}\right) . . . ( ii )$

Dividing (i) by (ii)

$4 = \dfrac{hc ( \dfrac{{\lambda}_{0} - \lambda}{\lambda{\lambda}_{0}} )}{hc\left(\dfrac{{\lambda}_{0} - 2\lambda}{2\lambda{\lambda}_{0}}\right)} ⇒ 4 = \dfrac{2 ( {\lambda}_{0} - \lambda )}{{\lambda}_{0} - 2\lambda} ⇒ 2{\lambda}_{0} = 6\lambda ⇒ {\lambda}_{0} = 3\lambda$

40445.text: There are three co-centric conducting spherical shells $A, B$ and $C$ of radii $a, b$ and $c$ respectively $(c>b>a)$ and they are charged with charge $q_{1}, q_{2}$ and $q_{3}$ respectively. The potentials of the spheres $A, B$ and $C$ respectively, are :
40445.sol:
The potential at any point due to a charged spherical shell of radius $R$ and charge $Q$ is $V = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_o} \frac{Q}{R}$ for points inside or on the surface ($r \le R$), and $V = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_o} \frac{Q}{r}$ for points outside ($r > R$).
Let $k = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_o}$. The potentials of the three shells $A, B, C$ with radii $a < b < c$ and charges $q_1, q_2, q_3$ are calculated by superposition.
For shell $A$ ($r = a$):
Shell $A$ is on its own surface, while it is inside shells $B$ and $C$.
$V_A = k\frac{q_1}{a} + k\frac{q_2}{b} + k\frac{q_3}{c} = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_o} \left( \frac{q_1}{a} + \frac{q_2}{b} + \frac{q_3}{c} \right)$
For shell $B$ ($r = b$):
Shell $B$ is outside shell $A$, on its own surface, and inside shell $C$.
$V_B = k\frac{q_1}{b} + k\frac{q_2}{b} + k\frac{q_3}{c} = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_o} \left( \frac{q_1 + q_2}{b} + \frac{q_3}{c} \right)$
For shell $C$ ($r = c$):
Shell $C$ is outside shells $A$ and $B$, and on its own surface.
$V_C = k\frac{q_1}{c} + k\frac{q_2}{c} + k\frac{q_3}{c} = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_o} \left( \frac{q_1 + q_2 + q_3}{c} \right)$
Comparing these expressions with the given options, option (3) matches correctly.

41892.text:
An air bubble of volume $2.9 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$ rises from the bottom of a swimming pool of 5 m deep. At the bottom of the pool water temperature is $17^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The volume of the bubble when it reaches the surface, where the water temperature is $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, is $\_\_\_\_ \mathrm{cm}^{3}$.
$\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\right.$, density of water $=10^{3} \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}, and $1 atm pressure is $\left.10^{5} \mathrm{~Pa}\right)$
41892.sol:
An air bubble rises through water with initial volume 2.9 cm³ at the bottom. Calculating pressures at both locations:
At bottom (5 m depth): $P_1 = P_{atm} + \rho gh = 10^5 + 10^3(10)(5) = 1.5 \times 10^5$ Pa
At surface: $P_2 = 10^5$ Pa
Initial temperature: $T_1 = 17°C = 290$ K, Final temperature: $T_2 = 27°C = 300$ K
Using ideal gas law: $\frac{P_1V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2V_2}{T_2}$
$V_2 = V_1 \times \frac{P_1}{P_2} \times \frac{T_2}{T_1} = 2.9 \times \frac{1.5 \times 10^5}{10^5} \times \frac{300}{290}$
$= 2.9 \times 1.5 \times \frac{30}{29} = 2.9 \times 1.5 \times 1.034 \approx 4.5$ cm³

55775.subject: Chemistry
55775.text: Which of the following molecules does not obey octet rule?
55775.sol:
The octet rule analysis proceeds by assessing the Lewis structure of each molecule, focusing on the central atom's electron count.

C$O_2$: The predicted structure is O=C=O. Carbon shares four bonds with oxygen, each oxygen retains two lone pairs, so oxygen has $2 + 3 \times 2 = 8$ electrons and carbon has $4 \times 2 = 8$ electrons—satisfying the octet rule.

CHCl_3$: Carbon forms single bonds with hydrogen and three chlorine atoms. Hydrogen has 2$ electrons from its bond, each chlorine has $1 \times 2 + 3 \times 2 = 8$ electrons, and carbon has $4 \times 2 = 8$ electrons—satisfying the octet rule.

ClF_3$: Chlorine forms three single bonds with fluorine atoms and bears two lone pairs. Each fluorine has 1 \times 2 + 3 \times 2 = 8$ electrons, but chlorine has $3 \times 2 + 2 \times 2 = 10$ electrons, exceeding the octet—violating the rule.

NH_3$: Nitrogen forms three single bonds with hydrogen atoms and holds one lone pair. Each hydrogen has 2$ electrons, nitrogen has $3 \times 2 + 2 = 8$ electrons—satisfying the octet rule.

Therefore, ClF_3$ does not obey the octet rule.

Final answer: $\boxed{C}$

$

56047.text: Nitric oxide reacts with $\mathrm{H}_2$ according to reaction, $2 \mathrm{NO}_{(\mathrm{g})}+2 \mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{ g})} \rightarrow \mathrm{N}_{2(\mathrm{ g})}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(\mathrm{g})}$, identify the correct relationship among the following.
56047.sol:
The balanced reaction is $2\mathrm{NO}_{(g)} + 2\mathrm{H}_{2(g)} \rightarrow \mathrm{N}_{2(g)} + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_{(g)}$.
For a general reaction $aA + bB \rightarrow cC + dD$, the rate is given by:

$\text{Rate} = -\frac{1}{a}\frac{d[A]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{b}\frac{d[B]}{dt} = +\frac{1}{c}\frac{d[C]}{dt} = +\frac{1}{d}\frac{d[D]}{dt}$

Applying this yields:

$\text{Rate} = -\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{NO}]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{H}_2]}{dt} = +\frac{d[\mathrm{N}_2]}{dt} = +\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}]}{dt}$

Option A states $-\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{NO}]}{dt} = \frac{d[\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}]}{dt}$, which contradicts the correct expression.

Option B states $-\frac{d[\mathrm{NO}]}{dt} = \frac{d[\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}]}{dt}$.
Multiplying the correct equality $-\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{NO}]}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}]}{dt}$ by 2 confirms this relationship.

Option C provides an incorrect coefficient.

Option D states $2\frac{d[\mathrm{H}_2]}{dt} = \frac{d[\mathrm{N}_2]}{dt}$, but from $-\frac{1}{2}\frac{d[\mathrm{H}_2]}{dt} = \frac{d[\mathrm{N}_2]}{dt}$, rearranging gives $\frac{d[\mathrm{H}_2]}{dt} = -2\frac{d[\mathrm{N}_2]}{dt}$, showing a sign and coefficient error.

The correct option is $\boxed{B}$.

56888.text: How long should aqueous NaCl be electrolysed by passing 100 ampere current, so that 0.5 mol chlorine is released at anode?
56888.sol:
For the electrolysis of aqueous NaCl, chlorine gas forms at the anode via the reaction:

$2\text{Cl}^- \rightarrow \text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{e}^-$

Releasing 0.5 mol of $\text{Cl}_2$ requires 1 mol of electrons from stoichiometry.

The total charge is then $Q = 1 \times 96500 = 96500\text{ C}$.

Given a current of 100 A, the required time is $t = \frac{96500}{100} = 965\text{ s}$.

Final Answer: $\boxed{C}$

57613.text: Identify the name of reaction that of aryl halide with alkyl halide and sodium metal in dry ether to give substituted aromatic compounds.
57613.sol:
The reaction involves coupling an aryl halide with an alkyl halide using sodium in dry ether to yield an alkyl-aryl product.

The Wurtz-Fittig reaction is defined by $Ar-X + R-X + 2Na $\xrightarrow{dry ether}$ Ar-R + 2NaX$, matching the given transformation.

Other reactions do not fit: the Wurtz reaction couples two alkyl halides (R-R'$), the Fittig reaction couples two aryl halides (Ar-Ar'$), and the Friedel-Crafts reaction uses Lewis acid catalysis rather than sodium metal.

59880.subject: Chemistry
59880.text: At $25\ ^{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ standard enthalpy of combustion of $\text{H}_2$, Cyclohexene and cyclohexane are -241, -3800 and -3920 kJ $\text{mol}^{-1}$ respectively. What is the heat of hydrogenation of cyclohexene?
59880.sol:
The hydrogenation reaction of cyclohexene is given by:

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10} + \text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$

The enthalpy of hydrogenation can be calculated using the standard enthalpies of combustion of the reactants and products:

$\Delta H = \sum \Delta H_c(\text{Reactants}) - \sum \Delta H_c(\text{Products})$

$\Delta H = \Delta H_c(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}) + \Delta H_c(\text{H}_2) - \Delta H_c(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12})$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta H = -3800 + (-241) - (-3920)$

$\Delta H = -4041 + 3920 = -121 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-121$ kJ

63496.text: There are 11 points in a plane of which 5 points are collinear. Then the total number of distinct quadrilaterals with vertices at these points is
63496.sol:
A quadrilateral requires selecting four points with no three collinear. Given 11 total points including five collinear, the valid selections are determined by excluding invalid cases.

The total ways to choose any four points is $C(11,4)=330$.

Invalid combinations occur if all four points are collinear, which gives $C(5,4)=5$ cases, or if three are collinear and one is not, yielding $C(5,3)\times C(6,1)=60$ cases.

Subtracting these from the total gives $330-5-60=265$ distinct quadrilaterals.

Answer: $\boxed{265}$

$\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2 = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ -1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } -2 \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } -2 \end{vmatrix} = 0\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$

Now, we find the scalar triple product $(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1) \cdot (\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2)$:

$(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1) \cdot (\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2) = (-4\hat{k}) \cdot (-4\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}) = 8 \neq 0$

Since the scalar triple product is non-zero, the shortest distance between the lines is non-zero. Also, the direction vectors are not proportional, meaning the lines are not parallel.

Therefore, the given lines are skew lines.

Answer: skew lines

64468.text: The angle between the lines $\frac{x-1}{l}=\frac{y+1}{m}=\frac{z}{n}$ and $\frac{x+1}{m}=\frac{y-3}{n}=\frac{z-1}{l}$, where $l > \mathrm{m} > \mathrm{n}$ and $\mathrm{l}, \mathrm{m}, \mathrm{n}$ are roots of the equation $x^3+x^2-4 x-4=0$, is

To find the angle between the lines, begin by solving the cubic equation $x^3 + x^2 - 4x - 4 = 0$. By factoring, this becomes $(x^2 - 4)(x + 1) = (x - 2)(x + 2)(x + 1)$ with roots $2$, $-2$, and $-1$.

Since $l > m > n$, assign $l = 2$, $m = -1$, and $n = -2$. The direction vectors of the lines are then: $\mathrm{d_1} = (2, -1, -2)$ and $\mathrm{d_2} = (-1, -2, 2)$.

The dot product $\mathrm{d_1} \cdot \mathrm{d_2} = 2 \cdot (-1) + (-1) \cdot (-2) + (-2) \cdot 2 = -4$, and both magnitudes equal $\sqrt{9} = 3$.

The cosine of the angle $\theta$ is therefore $\frac{-4}{9}$, giving $\theta = \cos^{-1} \left( \frac{-4}{9} \right), matching option B.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

64828.text: The number of solutions in $\left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ of the equation $\cos 3x \cdot \tan 5x = \sin 7x$ is
64828.sol:
Given equation: $\cos 3x \cdot \tan 5x = \sin 7x$

$\cos 3x \cdot \dfrac{\sin 5x}{\cos 5x} = \sin 7x$

$2 \sin 5x \cos 3x = 2 \sin 7x \cos 5x$

Using the identity $2 \sin A \cos B = \sin(A+B) + \sin(A-B)$:

$\sin 8x + \sin 2x = \sin 12x + \sin 2x$

$\sin 12x - \sin 8x = 0$

Using the identity $\sin C - \sin D = 2 \sin \left(\dfrac{C-D}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{C+D}{2}\right):

2 \sin 2x \cos 10x = 0$

This gives $\sin 2x = 0 or \cos 10x = 0$.

For $\sin 2x = 0$, $2x = $n\pi \Rightarrow$x = \dfrac{n\pi}{2}.

Since $ x \in $\left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right),$ the only solution is $x = 0$.

For $\cos 10x = 0$, $10x = (2k+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrowx = (2k+1)\dfrac{\pi}{20}.

Since $x \in $\left[0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}$\right)$, we have 0 \leq (2k+1)\dfrac{\pi}{20} < \dfrac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow$0 \leq 2k+1 < 10$.

The possible values for $2k+1$ are $1, 3, 5, 7, 9$.

This gives $x = $\dfrac{\pi}{20},\dfrac{3\pi}{20},\dfrac{5\pi}{20},\dfrac{7\pi}{20},\dfrac{9\pi}{20}$.

We must also ensure that \tan 5x$ is defined, which means $\cos 5x ≠ 0$.

$\cos 5x = 0 \Rightarrow 5x = (2m+1)$\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ \Rightarrow$ x = (4m+2)\dfrac{\pi}{20}$.

Since $2k+1$ is always odd and $4m+2$ is always even, none of our solutions make $\cos 5x = 0$.

Thus, all $1 + 5 = 6$ solutions are valid.

Answer: $6$

64940.sol:
Using the multiple angle formulas $\sin 3A = 3\sin A - 4\sin^3 A$ and $\cos 3A = 4\cos^3 A - 3\cos A$.

$\dfrac{\sin 3A}{\sin A} = 3 - 4\sin^2 A$

$\dfrac{\cos 3A}{\cos A} = 4\cos^2 A - 3$

Substituting these into the given expression:

$\left(\dfrac{\sin 3A}{\sin A}\right)^2 - \left(\dfrac{\cos 3A}{\cos A}\right)^2 = (3 - 4\sin^2 A)^2 - (4\cos^2 A - 3)^2$

Expanding the squares:

$= (9 - 24\sin^2 A + 16\sin^4 A) - (16\cos^4 A - 24\cos^2 A + 9)$

$= 16(\sin^4 A - \cos^4 A) - 24(\sin^2 A - \cos^2 A)$

Using a^2 - b^2 = (a-b)(a+b) and $\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A = 1$:

$= 16(\sin^2 A - \cos^2 A)(\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A) - 24(\sin^2 A - \cos^2 A)$

$= 16(\sin^2 A - \cos^2 A)(1) - 24(\sin^2 A - \cos^2 A)$

$= -8(\sin^2 A - \cos^2 A)$

$= 8(\cos^2 A - \sin^2 A)$

Since $\cos^2 A - \sin^2 A = \cos 2A$, the expression simplifies to:

$= 8\cos 2A$

Answer: $8\cos 2A$

66570.text: Graph shows variation of stopping potential with frequency of incident radiation on a metal plate. The value of Planck's constant is [$\mathrm{e}=$ charge on photoelectron]
66570.sol:
The photoelectric effect follows Einstein's photoelectric equation: $h u = \phi + K_\max$, where $h$ is Planck's constant, $ u$ is the frequency of incident radiation, $\phi$ is the work function, and $K_\max$ is the maximum kinetic energy.

Since $K_\max = eV_s$ where $e$ is the electronic charge, substitution gives: $h u = \phi + eV_s$.

Solving for $V_s$ yields the linear relation: $V_s = rac{h}{e} u - rac{\phi}{e}$.

This corresponds to a straight line with slope $m = h/e$. From the graph, the slope is calculated using two points: $m = (V_2 - V_1)/( u_2 - u_1)$.

Equating the expressions for slope: $h = e(V_2 - V_1)/( u_2 - u_1)$.

This matches the form of option C, assuming a typographical error where the denominator $V_2 - V_1$ was intended to be $ u_2 - u_1$.

66666.text: A photoelectric surface is illuminated successively by monochromatic light of wavelength ' $(\lambda)$ ' and ' $\left(\frac{\lambda}{2}\right)$. If the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons in the first case is one-third that in the second case, the work function of the surface of the material is ( $\mathrm{c}=$ speed of light, $\mathrm{h}=$ Planck's constant.)
66666.sol:
The correct option is (B).
Concept: Einstien's Photoelectric effect theory
The maximum kinetic energy $\mathrm{K}$ of the photoelectric electrons is related to the incident wavelength $\lambda$ and work function $\phi$ of the metal as follows:
$\mathrm{K}=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}-\phi$
For the incident wavelength $\lambda$, the equation is $\mathrm{K}=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}-\phi$
And for the incident wavelength $\frac{\lambda}{2}$, the equation is $3 K=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\frac{\lambda}{2}}-\phi$
Taking the ratio of two equations:
$\frac{1}{3}=\frac{\left(\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}-\phi\right)}{\left(\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\frac{\lambda}{2}}-\phi\right)}$
On solving, we get $\phi=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{2 \lambda}$

The magnetic field $B$ at the centre of a long solenoid is given by $B = \mu_0 n I$, where $n$ is the number of turns per unit length and $I$ is the current.

The magnetic field intensity $H$ is related to the magnetic field $B$ in free space by the relation $H = \dfrac{B}{\mu_0}$.

Substituting the value of $B$, we get $H = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I}{\mu_0} = nI$.

Answer: $nI$

The total energy E of a simple pendulum with small angular amplitude $\theta_0$ and length L is $E = \frac{1}{2} m g L \theta_0^2$.

Cancelling common factors $M_1 g L_2$ yields $2\theta_{0A}^2 = \theta_{0B}^2$, so $\theta_{0B} = \sqrt{2} \theta_{0A}$.

The linear amplitudes relate as $A = L\theta_0$, giving $A_A = 2L_2\theta_{0A}$ and $A_B = L_2\cdot\sqrt{2}\theta_{0A}$.

The ratio is $\frac{A_B}{A_A} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707$, showing $A_B < A_A$.

71945.text: In a compound, atoms of element Y form hexagonal close-packed structure. Atoms of element X occupy $2/3$ of the octahedral voids. What is the formula of the compound?
71945.sol:
Let the number of atoms of element Y forming the hexagonal close-packed (hcp) lattice be $N$.

The number of octahedral voids in a close-packed structure is equal to the number of atoms forming the lattice, which is $N$.

Since atoms of element X occupy $\dfrac{2}{3}$ of the octahedral voids, the number of atoms of X is $\dfrac{2}{3}N$.

The ratio of the number of atoms of X to that of Y is $\dfrac{2}{3}N : N = 2 : 3$.

Thus, the formula of the compound is $\text{X}_2\text{Y}_3$.

Answer: $\text{X}_2\text{Y}_3$

72021.subject: Chemistry
72021.text: Calculate the energy per mole of photons of red light with a wavelength $750$ nm. [h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}$ Js, $C = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s.]$
72021.sol:
The energy of a single photon is given by $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$.

The energy of one mole of photons is $E_{mole} = N_A \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$, where $N_A$ is Avogadro's number ($6.022 \times 10^{23}$ mol$^{-1}$).

Given:
$\lambda = 750 \text{ nm} = 750 \times 10^{-9}$ m
$h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}$ J s
$c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s

Substituting the values into the formula:

$E_{mole} = \dfrac{6.022 \times 10^{23} \times 6.626 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{750 \times 10^{-9}}$

$E_{mole} = \dfrac{119.7 \times 10^{-3}}{750 \times 10^{-9}}$

$E_{mole} = 0.1596 \times 10^6 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$

$E_{mole} = 1.596 \times 10^5 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $1.596 \times 10^5$ J.

72380.subject: Physics
72380.text: Which of the following gives output $0$ in the NAND gate?
72380.sol:
The Boolean expression for a NAND gate is $Y = \overline{A \cdot B}$.

For $A = 1$, $B = 0$, $Y = \overline{1 \cdot 0} = \overline{0} = 1$

For $A = 1$, $B = 1$, $Y = \overline{1 \cdot 1} = \overline{1} = 0$

For $A = 0$, $B = 0$, $Y = \overline{0 \cdot 0} = \overline{0} = 1$

For $A = 0$, $B = 1$, $Y = \overline{0 \cdot 1} = \overline{0} = 1$

The output is $0$ when $A = 1$ and $B = 1$.

Answer: $A = 1$, $B = 1$

72429.subject: Physics
72429.text: For an isochoric process, which of the following statements is NOT true?
72429.sol:
An isochoric process is a thermodynamic process in which the volume of the system remains constant.

Since the volume is constant, the change in volume is zero, so $\Delta V = 0$.

The work done by the gas is given by $W = P \Delta V$. Since $\Delta V = 0$, the work done is $W = 0$.

According to the first law of thermodynamics, $Q = \Delta U + W$. Substituting $W = 0$, we get $Q = \Delta U$.

In an isochoric process, the temperature can change (for example, when heat is added to a gas in a rigid container, its temperature and pressure increase). Therefore, $\Delta T = 0$ is not generally true for an isochoric process (it is true for an isothermal process).

Answer: $\Delta T = 0$

76686.subject: Mathematics
76686.text: Let $z_1 and z_2$ be two complex numbers such that $\left|\frac{z_1+z_2}{z_1-z_2}\right|=1$, then what is $\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right)+1$ equal to?
76686.sol:
Let $z_1=x_1+i y_1 and z_2=x_2+i y_2$
Now, $\quad\left|\frac{z_1+z_2}{z_1-z_2}\right|=1\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad\left|z_1+z_2\right|=\left|z_1-z_2\right| \\
& \Rightarrow\left|\left(x_1+x_2\right)+i\left(y_1+y_2\right)\right|=\mid\left(x_1-x_2\right) \\
& +i\left(y_1-y_2\right) \mid \\
& \Rightarrow\left(x_1+x_2\right)^2+\left(y_1+y_2\right)^2=\left(x_1-x_2\right)^2 \\
& +\left(y_1-y_2\right)^2 \\
& \Rightarrow x_1^2+x_2^2+2 x_1 x_2+y_1^2+y_2^2+2 y_1 y_2 \\
& =x_1^2+x_2^2-2 x_1 x_2+y_1^2 \\
& +y_2^2-2 y_1 y_2 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x_1 x_2+y_1 y_2=0 \\
& \frac{z_1}{z_2}=\frac{x_1+i y_1}{x_2+i y_2} \times \frac{x_2-i y_2}{x_2-i y_2} \\
& =\frac{\left(x_1 x_2+y_1 y_2\right)+i\left(y_1 x_2-x_1 y_2\right)}{x_2^2+y_2^2} \\
& =0+\frac{i\left(y_1 x_2-x_1 y_2\right)}{x_2^2+y_2^2}
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right)=0 \\ & \therefore \quad \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right)+1=1.\end{aligned}$

78671.subject: Mathematics
78671.text: The mean of the series $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$ is $\overline{\mathrm{X}}$. If $\mathrm{x}_2$ is replaced by $\lambda$, then what is the new mean?
78671.sol:
Mean of series $\left(x_1, x_2, x_3 \ldots \ldots x_{\mathrm{n}}\right)\begin{aligned}
& \bar{x}=\frac{x_1+x_2+x_3+\ldots . x_n}{n} \\
& \Rightarrow x_1+x_2+x_3+\ldots . x_n=n \bar{x}
\end{aligned}$
Now we will replace $x_2$ by $\lambda$ so no. of elements in series will not change.
New series will include $\lambda$ and exclude $x_2$
Hence new series sum :
$\left(x_1+x_2+\ldots . . x_n\right)-x_2+\lambda=n \bar{x}+\lambda-x_2$
Now new mean $=\frac{n \bar{x}+\lambda-x_2}{n}=\frac{n \bar{x}-x_2+\lambda}{n}$

Direction ratios of the line from the point (1, -1, 2) to the given plane is $\langle 3,2,2\rangle\therefore \quad \frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y+1}{2}=\frac{z-2}{2}=\lambda$ Co-ordinates any points on the line PQ are $\begin{aligned} & x=3 \lambda+1, y=2 \lambda-1, z=2 \lambda+2 \\ & x+2 y+3 z=18 \\ & \therefore \quad 3 \lambda+1+4 \lambda-2+6 \lambda+6=18 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 13 \lambda+5=18 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 13 \lambda=13 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \lambda \end{aligned}$ Hence, the co-ordinates of Q are $(3+1,2-1,2+2)=(4,1,4)$

79253.text: For any vector $\vec{r}$, what is $(\vec{r} \cdot \hat{i})(\vec{r} \times \hat{i})+(\vec{r} \cdot \hat{j})(\vec{r} \times \hat{j})+(\vec{r} \cdot \hat{k})(\vec{r} \times \hat{k})$ equal to?
79253.sol:
$(\vec{r} \cdot \hat{i})(\vec{r} \times \hat{i})+(\vec{r} \cdot \hat{j})(\vec{r} \times \hat{j})+(\vec{r} \cdot \hat{k})(\vec{r} \times \hat{k})$ ...(i)
We have,
$\begin{aligned} \vec{r} & =a \hat{i}+b \hat{j}+c \hat{k} \\ (\vec{r} \hat{i}) & =(a \hat{i}+b \hat{j}+c \hat{k}) \cdot \hat{i}=a \\ (\vec{r} \cdot \hat{j}) & =b \\ (\vec{r} \cdot \hat{k}) & =c\end{aligned}$ and $\qquad \vec{r} \times \hat{i}=\left|\begin{array}{lll}
\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\
a & b & c \\
1 & 0 & 0
\end{array}$\right|=-\hat{j}(-c)-b \hat{k}=c \hat{j}-b \hat{k}$
Similarly, $\quad $\vec{r}$ \times \hat{j}=-c \hat{i}+a \hat{k}$
and\vec{r} \hat{k}=b \hat{i}-a \hat{j}$
Putting these values in (i) we get
$\begin{aligned}
& a(\hat{j}-b \hat{k})+b(-c \hat{i}+a \hat{k})+c(b \hat{i}-a \hat{j}) \\
&=a c \hat{j}-a b \hat{k}-b c \hat{i}+a b \hat{k}+b c \hat{i}-a c \hat{j}=0
\end{aligned}$

82343.subject: Physics
82343.text: A galvanometer of resistance $100\ \Omega$ gives full scale deflection for a current of $1$ mA. It is converted into an ammeter of range $0 - 10$ A. The shunt required is :
82343.sol:
Given $G = 100\ \Omega$, $I_g = 1\text{ mA} = 10^{-3}\text{ A}$, and $I = 10\text{ A}$.

The shunt resistance $S$ required to convert a galvanometer into an ammeter is given by:

$S = \dfrac{I_g G}{I - I_g}$

Substituting the values:

$S = \dfrac{10^{-3} \times 100}{10 - 10^{-3}}$

Since $10 \gg 10^{-3}$, we can approximate $10 - 10^{-3} \approx 10$.

$S \approx \dfrac{0.1}{10} = 0.01\ \Omega$

Answer: $0.01\ \Omega$

83151.subject: Physics
83151.text: A particle moves along a straight line $\mathrm{OX}$. At a time $t$ (in seconds) the distance $x$ (in metres) of the particle from $\mathrm{O}$ is given by $x=40+12 t-t^3$. How long would the particle travel before coming to rest ?
83151.sol:
The given equation is
$x=40+127-t^3$
Differentiating we get
$u=\frac{d x}{d t}=12-3 t^2$
When particle comes to rest means
$\begin{array}{l} 
& v = 0 \\
& 12-3 t^2 =0 \\
& t =2 \mathrm{sec} .
\end{array}$
The distance travelled before coming to rest
$\begin{aligned}
\int_0^5 d s & ={ }_0^2 v d t \\
5 & =\int_0^2\left(12-3 t^2\right) d t \\
& =\left[12 t-\frac{3 t^3}{3}\right]_0^2 \\
& =12 \times 2-(8-0) \\
& =16 \mathrm{~m} .
\end{aligned}$

84563.text: In which of the animal dimorphic nucleus is found?
84563.sol:
Paramecium is heterokaryotic i.e., it possesses a dimorphic nuclear apparatus - a single large macronucleus which controls metabolism and one or more small micronuclei concerned with reproduction.
Related Theory
Heterokaryotic refers to cells where two or more genetically different nuclei share one common cytoplasm. This is the stage after Plasmogamy, the fusion of the cytoplasm, and before Karyogamy, the fusion of the nuclei.

85203.sol: For the ABO system of blood groups, allele IA produces N acetylgalactosamyl transferase enzyme which recognizes H antigen present in RBC membrane and adds N-acetylgalactosamine to sugar part of H antigen to form A antigen. 85223.subject: Zoology
85223.text: Chromosomal theory of inheritance was proposed by:
85223.sol:
Chromosomal theory of inheritance was independently given by Sutton and Boveri in 1902. The two workers found a close similarly between the transmission of hereditary traits and behaviour of chromosomes while passing from generation to the next through the agency of gametes. Sutton united the knowledge of chromosomal segregation with Mendelian principles and called it the chromosomal theory of inheritance.

T.H. Morgan gave experimental verification to this.

85335.sol:
Mendel studied the following genes (the dominant trait is given first).
Chromosome 1: Purple/white flowers; Yellow/green peas.
Chromosome 4: Axial/terminal flowers; Tall/short plant; Inflated/ constricted pods.
Chromosome 5: green/yellow pods.
Chromosome 7: Round/wrinkled seeds
Related Theory
Mendel studied inheritance in peas (Pisum sativum). He chose peas because they had been used for similar studies, are easy to grow and can be sown each year. Pea flowers contain both male and female parts, called stamen and stigma, and usually selfpollinate.

89155.text: In a compound oxide ion have ccp arrangement, cations A are present in $\dfrac{1}{8}$ of the tetrahedral voids and cations B occupy $\dfrac{1}{2}$ of the octahedral voids. What are the formula of the compound?
89155.sol:
Oxide ions are forming the lattice
Effective number of oxide ions $= 4 \left(ccp\right)$
$∴$ Tetrahedral voids $= 2 \times4 = 8$
And effective number of A atom $= \dfrac{1}{8} \times8 = 1$
Number of octahedral voids $= 4$
Effective number of B atom $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times4 = 2$
$∴$ Molecular formulae $= A{B}_{2}{O}_{4}$

Vertical velocity of the ball just before each collision is

The height up to which the ball bounces after each collision is

$h^{'} = h - d$

Vertical velocity of the ball just after the collision is

${v}_{sep} = e{v}_{app} = e\sqrt{2gh}$

Using the principle of conservation of mechanical energy we get

$\dfrac{1}{2}$ m{ \lleft(e\sqrt{2gh}\right)}^{2} = mg $\left(h - d\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{2} e^{2} \left(2gh\right) =$ g $\left(h - d\right)$

$e^{2}h = h - d$

$d = h \left(1 - e^{2}\right)$

$h = \dfrac{d}{1 - e^{2}}$

$$

100098.subject: Physics
100098.text: A physical quantity $X$ is defined by the relation $X = \dfrac{a b^2}{c + d^2}$. It is given that $X$ has the dimensions of pressure, $a$ has the dimensions of force, and $c$ has the dimensions of length. The dimensional formula of the ratio $\dfrac{b}{d}$ is:
100098.sol:
According to the principle of homogeneity of dimensions, quantities added together must have the same dimensions. From the denominator $(c + d^2)$:
$[d^2] = [c] = [\mathrm{L}]$
$[d] = [\mathrm{L}^{1/2}]$

The dimensional formula of the entire equation is:
$[X] = \dfrac{[a][b^2]}{[c]}$

We are given that $X$ is pressure and $a$ is force. Substituting their dimensional formulas:
$[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^{-1} \mathrm{T}^{-2}] = \dfrac{[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L} \mathrm{T}^{-2}][b^2]}{[\mathrm{L}]}$

Simplifying the right side:
$[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^{-1} \mathrm{T}^{-2}] = [\mathrm{M} \mathrm{T}^{-2}][b^2]$

Solving for $[b^2]$:
$[b^2] = \dfrac{[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{L}^{-1} \mathrm{T}^{-2}]}{[\mathrm{M} \mathrm{T}^{-2}]} = [\mathrm{L}^{-1}]$
$[b] = [\mathrm{L}^{-1/2}]$

The dimensional formula of the ratio $\dfrac{b}{d}$ is:
$\left[\dfrac{b}{d}\right] = \dfrac{[\mathrm{L}^{-1/2}]}{[\mathrm{L}^{1/2}]} = [\mathrm{L}^{-1}]$

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{L}^{-1}\right]$

100158.subject: Physics
100158.text: Which of the following pairs does not have same dimensions ?
options: moment of inertia and moment of force
100158.sol:
Impulse $=F \times t$
$$
=\frac{m\left(v_2-v_1\right)}{t} \times t=m\left(v_2-v_1\right)
$$
$=$ change in momentum
$\therefore \quad$ [Impulse $]=[$ Momentum $]$
Angular momentum, $\mathrm{L}=m v r$
Planck's constant, $[h]=[$ energy $] \times[$ time $]$
$$
\Rightarrow[F \times r \times \text{ time })=\frac{m\left(v_2-v_1\right)}{t} \times r \times t
$$
$\Rightarrow m\left(v_2-v_1\right) \times r=($ change of momentum $) \times r$
$\therefore \quad[h]=[L]$.
Work, $W=\vec{F} \cdot \vec{d}:$ Torque, $\tau=\vec{r} \times \vec{F}$
$$
\therefore \quad[W]=[\tau]
$$
Moment of inertia, $I=m r^2=\operatorname{mass} \times(\text{ distance })^2$

Moment of force, $\tau=\vec{r} \times \vec{F}=$ distance $\times$ force
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \quad=\text{ distance } \times \frac{\text{ change of momentum }}{\text{ time }} \\
& \therefore \quad[\mathrm{I}] \neq[\tau] .
\end{aligned}
$$
Therefore, moment of inertia and moment of force have different dimensions.

101700.subject: Physics
101700.text: The variation of gauge pressure ($P$) with depth ($h$) for two different liquids A and B is plotted on a graph. The straight line for liquid A makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the $h$-axis, while the line for liquid B makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the $h$-axis. What is the ratio of the density of liquid A to that of liquid B?
101700.sol:
Gauge pressure at a depth $h$ in a liquid of density $\rho$ is given by $P = \rho gh$.

Rearranging this equation, we get $\dfrac{P}{h} = \rho g$.

On a graph of $P$ (y-axis) versus $h$ (x-axis), the slope of the line is equal to $\dfrac{P}{h}$. Therefore, the slope is directly proportional to the density of the liquid ($\text{Slope} = \rho g$).

For liquid A, the slope is $\tan(60^\circ) = \sqrt{3}$.

For liquid B, the slope is $\tan(30^\circ) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

The ratio of their densities is:
$\dfrac{\rho_A}{\rho_B} = \dfrac{\text{Slope}_A}{\text{Slope}_B} = \dfrac{\tan(60^\circ)}{\tan(30^\circ)} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}} = 3$

Thus, the ratio of the density of liquid A to liquid B is $3:1$.

Answer: $3:1$

102918.subject: Physics
102918.text: An uncharged solid spherical conductor contains a cavity within it. A point charge $+Q$ is placed inside the cavity without touching its walls. What will be the induced charges on the inner surface of the cavity and the outer surface of the conductor, respectively?
102918.sol:
Consider a Gaussian surface entirely within the solid material of the conductor, enclosing the cavity. In electrostatic equilibrium, the electric field inside the conducting material is zero everywhere.

According to Gauss's law, the net flux through this surface is zero, which means the net charge enclosed must be zero. Therefore, an induced charge of $-Q$ must appear on the inner surface of the cavity to exactly cancel the $+Q$ point charge inside.

Since the conductor is initially uncharged and isolated, its total charge must remain zero. By conservation of charge, the sum of the charges on the inner and outer surfaces must be zero. Thus, a charge of $+Q$ must appear on the outer surface of the conductor.

Answer: $-Q$ and $+Q$

103904.subject: Physics
103904.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The induced EMF between the centre and the rim of a metallic wheel rotating in a uniform magnetic field remains unchanged if the number of identical metallic spokes is increased.

Reason (R): The metallic spokes act as identical sources of EMF connected in parallel between the centre and the rim.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
103904.sol:
When a metallic wheel with spokes rotates in a uniform magnetic field, each spoke acts as a source of motional EMF of magnitude $\varepsilon = \dfrac{1}{2} B \omega r^2$.

All the spokes are connected between the same two points: the centre of the wheel and its metallic rim. In an electrical circuit, when identical sources of EMF are connected in parallel, the equivalent EMF of the combination is equal to the EMF of a single source.

Therefore, increasing the number of spokes does not change the net induced EMF between the centre and the rim. Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) correctly explains (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

104498.subject: Physics
104498.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I describes different optical configurations involving glass lenses ($\mu = 1.5$) with a radius of curvature of $20\text{ cm}$ for their curved surfaces. List-II gives the equivalent focal length of the system.

List-IList-II
(A) An equiconvex lens in air(I) $+10\text{ cm}$
(B) Two such equiconvex lenses placed in contact in air(II) $-100\text{ cm}$
(C) Two plano-convex lenses placed with their curved surfaces facing each other, and the gap filled with a liquid of $\mu = 1.6$(III) Infinity
(D) The equiconvex lens completely immersed in a liquid of $\mu = 1.5$(IV) $+20\text{ cm}$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
104498.sol:
(A) For the equiconvex lens in air:
$\dfrac{1}{f_A} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{-R}\right) = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{2}{20}\right) = \dfrac{1}{20}\text{ cm}^{-1} \Rightarrow f_A = +20\text{ cm}$.

(B) For two such lenses in contact:
$\dfrac{1}{f_B} = \dfrac{1}{f_A} + \dfrac{1}{f_A} = \dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{2}{20} = \dfrac{1}{10}\text{ cm}^{-1} \Rightarrow f_B = +10\text{ cm}$.

(C) The combination consists of two plano-convex lenses and a biconcave liquid lens in the middle.
Focal length of each plano-convex lens: $\dfrac{1}{f_p} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{20}\right) = \dfrac{1}{40}\text{ cm}^{-1}$.
Focal length of the liquid lens: $\dfrac{1}{f_L} = (1.6 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{-20} - \dfrac{1}{20}\right) = 0.6 \times \left(-\dfrac{2}{20}\right) = -\dfrac{6}{100}\text{ cm}^{-1}$.
Equivalent focal length: $\dfrac{1}{f_C} = \dfrac{1}{f_p} + \dfrac{1}{f_L} + \dfrac{1}{f_p} = \dfrac{1}{40} - \dfrac{6}{100} + \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{6}{100} = \dfrac{5 - 6}{100} = -\dfrac{1}{100}\text{ cm}^{-1} \Rightarrow f_C = -100\text{ cm}$.

(D) When immersed in a liquid of the same refractive index ($\mu = 1.5$):
$\dfrac{1}{f_D} = \left(\dfrac{1.5}{1.5} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{2}{20}\right) = 0 \Rightarrow f_D = \infty$.

Hence, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)

105578.subject: Physics
105578.text:
An electron of mass $m$ and a photon have the same de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$. The ratio of the kinetic energy of the electron to the energy of the photon is :
(Take $c$ as the speed of light and $h$ as Planck's constant)
105578.sol:
Since the electron and the photon have the same de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$, they possess the same linear momentum $p$.

The momentum is given by:
$p = \dfrac{h}{\lambda}$

The kinetic energy of the electron $E_e$ is related to its momentum by:
$E_e = \dfrac{p^2}{2m} = \dfrac{h^2}{2m\lambda^2}$

The energy of the photon $E_{ph}$ is related to its momentum by:
$E_{ph} = pc = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$

Taking the ratio of the kinetic energy of the electron to the energy of the photon:
$\dfrac{E_e}{E_{ph}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{h^2}{2m\lambda^2}}{\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}} = \dfrac{h}{2mc\lambda}$

Answer: $\dfrac{h}{2mc\lambda}$

105887.subject: Chemistry
105887.text:
What is the total number of electrons present in $1.6 \text{ g}$ of methane ($\text{CH}_4$)?
(Given: Atomic masses of $\text{C} = 12 \text{ u}$, $\text{H} = 1 \text{ u}$; $N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23} \text{ mol}^{-1}$)
105887.sol:
Molar mass of $\text{CH}_4 = 12 + 4 \times 1 = 16 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

Number of moles of $\text{CH}_4 = \dfrac{1.6 \text{ g}}{16 \text{ g mol}^{-1}} = 0.1 \text{ mol}$.

Number of $\text{CH}_4$ molecules $= 0.1 \times N_A = 0.1 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 6.022 \times 10^{22}$.

One molecule of $\text{CH}_4$ contains $6$ electrons from carbon and $1$ electron from each of the $4$ hydrogen atoms, giving a total of $6 + 4 = 10$ electrons.

Total number of electrons $= 10 \times 6.022 \times 10^{22} = 6.022 \times 10^{23}$.

Answer: $6.022 \times 10^{23}$

108963.subject: Chemistry
108963.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For the reaction $2\mathrm{SO}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_{3(\mathrm{g})}$, the ratio $\dfrac{K_p}{K_c}$ decreases as temperature increases.

Reason (R): For this reaction, the number of moles of gaseous products is greater than the number of moles of gaseous reactants ($\Delta n_g > 0$).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
108963.sol:
For the given reaction $2\mathrm{SO}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{SO}_{3(\mathrm{g})}$:
$\Delta n_g = (\text{moles of gaseous products}) - (\text{moles of gaseous reactants})$
$\Delta n_g = 2 - (2 + 1) = -1$

Since $\Delta n_g < 0$, the Reason (R) is false.

The relationship between $K_p$ and $K_c$ is:
$K_p = K_c(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta n_g}$
$\dfrac{K_p}{K_c} = (\mathrm{RT})^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{\mathrm{RT}}$

As temperature ($\mathrm{T}$) increases, the value of $\mathrm{RT}$ increases, which causes the ratio $\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{RT}}$ to decrease. Therefore, the ratio $\dfrac{K_p}{K_c}$ decreases with an increase in temperature. Thus, the Assertion (A) is true.

Hence, Assertion is true but Reason is false.

Answer: Assertion is true but Reason is false.

114377.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) $F_2$(I) Strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution
(B) $Li$(II) Standard reference electrode with $0.00\text{ V}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
114377.sol:
According to the electrochemical series:

Fluorine ($F_2$) has the highest standard reduction potential ($+2.87\text{ V}$), making it the strongest oxidizing agent.

Lithium ($Li$) has the lowest standard reduction potential ($-3.05\text{ V}$), making it the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solutions.

The Standard Hydrogen Electrode ($H^+$) is assigned a standard reduction potential of exactly $0.00\text{ V}$.

Zinc ($Zn$) has a standard reduction potential of $-0.76\text{ V}$, which is lower than that of Copper ($+0.34\text{ V}$) but higher than that of Magnesium ($-2.36\text{ V}$). Therefore, $Zn$ can reduce $Cu^{2+}$ but cannot reduce $Mg^{2+}$.

Thus, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)

117105.subject: Chemistry
117105.text:
Match List I with List II.

List I (Ion)List II (Spin-only magnetic moment)
(A) $\mathrm{Ti}^{3+}$ (Z = 22)(I) $0 \text{ BM}$
(B) $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ (Z = 27)(II) $1.73 \text{ BM}$
(C) $\mathrm{Gd}^{3+}$ (Z = 64)(III) $3.87 \text{ BM}$
(D) $\mathrm{Lu}^{3+}$ (Z = 71)(IV) $7.9 \text{ BM}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
117105.sol:
The spin-only magnetic moment is calculated using the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$, where n is the number of unpaired electrons.

(A) $\mathrm{Ti}^{3+}$ (Z = 22): Configuration is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3\mathrm{d}^{1}$. Number of unpaired electrons (n) = 1. $\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73 \text{ BM}$.

(B) $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ (Z = 27): Configuration is $[\mathrm{Ar}] 3\mathrm{d}^{7}$. Number of unpaired electrons (n) = 3. $\mu = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87 \text{ BM}$.

(C) $\mathrm{Gd}^{3+}$ (Z = 64): Configuration is $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^{7}$. Number of unpaired electrons (n) = 7. $\mu = \sqrt{7(7+2)} = \sqrt{63} \approx 7.9 \text{ BM}$.

(D) $\mathrm{Lu}^{3+}$ (Z = 71): Configuration is $[\mathrm{Xe}] 4\mathrm{f}^{14}$. Number of unpaired electrons (n) = 0. $\mu = \sqrt{0(0+2)} = 0 \text{ BM}$.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)

117817.text: What are the oxidation state and coordination number of the central metal ion in the complex $[Cr(EDTA)]^{-}$? (where EDTA is ethylenediaminetetraacetate)
117817.sol:
Let the oxidation state of Cr be $x$.

The ligand EDTA (ethylenediaminetetraacetate) carries a charge of $-4$.

The sum of oxidation states must equal the net charge on the complex ion:
$x + (-4) = -1$
$x = +3$

EDTA is a hexadentate ligand, meaning it forms 6 coordinate bonds with the central metal ion (through two nitrogen and four oxygen donor atoms).

Therefore, the coordination number of Cr in this complex is 6.

The oxidation state is +3 and the coordination number is 6.

Answer: +3 and 6

options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
118791.sol:
Assertion (A) is false. 2-Methylpropan-1-ol (isobutyl alcohol) is a primary (1$^{\circ}$) alcohol. Primary alcohols do not produce turbidity with Lucas reagent at room temperature because the primary carbocation intermediate is highly unstable.

Reason (R) is true. The Lucas test proceeds via an S$_N$1 mechanism. Tertiary alcohols react instantaneously to give turbidity because they form highly stable tertiary carbocations, making the reaction very fast.

Therefore, (A) is false but (R) is true.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true

When cyclohexanone undergoes aldol condensation in the presence of a base, it will produce a β− hydroxy ketone.

When cyclohexanone undergoes aldol condensation followed by heating, the product formed is represented by the option (b).

121704.subject: Botany
121704.text: In which habitat is algae not explicitly mentioned to occur?
121704.sol: Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic (both freshwater and marine) organisms. <mark>They occur in a variety of other habitats: moist stones, soils and wood</mark>. Some of them also occur in association with fungi (lichen) and animals (e.g., on sloth bear). The form and size of algae is highly variable, ranging from colonial forms like Volvox and the filamentous forms like Ulothrix and Spirogyra (Figure 3.1). A few of the marine forms such as kelps, form massive plant bodies.The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina, is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus.

121760.subject: Botany
121760.text: Floridean starch is similar in structure to which of the following substances?
121760.sol: The members of rhodophyceae are commonly called red algae because of the predominance of the red pigment, r-phycoerythrin in their body. Majority of the red algae are marine with greater concentrations found in the warmer areas. They occur in both well-lighted regions close to the surface of water and also at great depths in oceans where relatively little light penetrates.The red thalli of most of the red algae are multicellular. Some of them have complex body organization. <mark>The food is stored as floridean starch which is very similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure.</mark> The red algae usually reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation. They reproduce asexually by non-motile spores and sexually by non-motile gametes. Sexual reproduction is oogamous and accompanied by complex post fertilization developments. The common members are: Polysiphonia, Porphyra, Gracilaria and Gelidium.

121785.subject: Botany
121785.text: What effect do mosses have on soil erosion?
options: They have no effect on soil erosion.
They cause soil erosion in dry areas.
121785.sol: Bryophytes in general are of little economic importance but some mosses provide food for herbaceous mammals, birds and other animals. Species of Sphagnum, a moss, provide peat that have long been used as fuel, and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material because of their capacity to hold water. Mosses along with lichens are the first organisms to colonize rocks and hence, are of great ecological importance. They decompose rocks making the substrate suitable for the growth of higher plants. <mark>Since moses form dense mats on the soil, they reduce the impact of falling rain and prevent soil erosion.</mark> The bryophytes are divided into liverworts and mosses.Zygote thereafter produces a multicellular well-differentiated sporophyte which is the dominant phase of the pteridophytes. In the majority of the pteridophytes all the spores are of similar kinds; such plants are called homosporous. Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores, are known as heterosporous. The megaspores and microspores germinate and give rise to female and male gametophytes, respectively.

122536.text:
Read the following statements regarding the animal Psittacula:
(A) It is a homoiothermous animal.
(B) Its digestive tract has additional chambers, the crop and gizzard.
(C) Its heart is three-chambered.
(D) Its long bones are hollow with air cavities.
(E) It is a viviparous animal with internal fertilisation.

How many of the above statements are correct?
122536.sol:
Psittacula is the scientific name for the parrot, which belongs to the class Aves.

Statement (A) is correct: Birds are homoiothermous (warm-blooded) animals.

Statement (B) is correct: The digestive tract of birds has additional chambers, the crop and gizzard.

Statement (C) is incorrect: Birds have a completely four-chambered heart, not three-chambered.

Statement (D) is correct: The endoskeleton is fully ossified and the long bones are hollow with air cavities (pneumatic).

Statement (E) is incorrect: Although fertilisation is internal, birds are oviparous (egg-laying), not viviparous.

Therefore, exactly three statements ((A), (B), and (D)) are correct.

Answer: Three

123633.subject: Botany
123633.text: How do animal cells undergo cytokinesis?
options: By the appearance of a furrow in the plasma membrane
By the formation of a simple precursor called the cell-plate
By the formation of a new cell wall that grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls
By the formation of a syncytium
123633.sol: In an animal cell, this is achieved by the appearance of a furrow in the plasma membrane. The furrow gradually deepens and ultimately joins in the centre dividing the cell cytoplasm into two. Plant cells however, are enclosed by a relatively inextensible cell wall, thererfore they undergo cytokinesis by a different mechanism. In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls. The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor, called the cell-plate that represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells. At the time of cytoplasmic division, organelles like mitochondria and plastids get distributed between the two daughter cells.
123633.meta: How do animal cells undergo cytokinesis?

123644.subject: Botany
123644.text: What is the significance of mitosis in the life of an organism?
options: Mitosis results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement.
Mitosis is essential for the cell to divide to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio.
Mitosis is a process that occurs only in diploid cells.
Mitosis is only important in the growth of multicellular organisms.
123644.sol: Mitosis usually results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement. Cell growth results in disturbing the ratio between the nucleus and the cytoplasm. It therefore becomes essential for the cell to divide to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio. A very significant contribution of mitosis is cell repair. The cells of the upper layer of the epidermis, cells of the lining of the gut, and blood cells are being constantly replaced. Mitotic divisions in the meristematic tissues – the apical and the lateral cambium, result in a continuous growth of plants throughout their life.

127880.subject: Zoology
127880.text: How do cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems contribute to the survival of the body?
127880.sol: In the preceding chapters you came across a large variety of organisms, both unicellular and multicellular, of the animal kingdom. In unicellular organisms, all functions like digestion, respiration and reproduction are performed by a single cell. In the complex body of multicellular animals the same basic functions are carried out by different groups of cells in a well organised manner. The body of a simple organism like Hydra is made of different types of cells and the number of cells in each type can be in thousands. The human body is composed of billions of cells to perform various functions. How do these cells in the body work together? As you have already learnt in your earlier classes, in multicellular animals, a group of similar cells alongwith intercellular substances perform a specific function. Such an organisation is called tissue. You may be surprised to know that all complex animals consist of only four basic types of tissues. These tissues are organised in specific proportion and pattern to form an organ like stomach, lung, heart and kidney. When two or more organs perform a common function by their physical and/or chemical interaction, they together form organ system, e.g., digestive system, respiratory system, etc. Cells, tissues, organs and organ systems split up the work in a way that exhibits division of labour and contribute to the survival of the body as a whole.

127904.subject: Zoology
127904.text: What makes the skin of a frog smooth and slippery?
127904.sol: Have you ever touched the skin of frog? The skin is smooth and slippery due to the presence of mucus. The skin is always maintained in a moist condition. The colour of dorsal side of body is generally olive green with dark irregular spots. On the ventral side the skin is uniformly pale yellow. The frog never drinks water but absorb it through the skin. Body of a frog is divisible into head and trunk A neck and tail are absent. Above the mouth, a pair of nostrils is present. Eyes are bulged and covered by a nictitating membrane that protects them while in water. On either side of eyes a membranous tympanum (ear) receives sound signals. The forelimbs and hind limbs help in swimming, walking, leaping and burrowing. The hind limbs end in five digits and they are larger and muscular than fore limbs that end in four digits. Feet have webbed digits that help in swimming. Frogs exhibit sexual dimorphism. Male frogs can be distinguished by the presence of sound producing vocal sacs and also a copulatory pad on the first digit of the fore limbs which are absent in female frogs.

128614.subject: Zoology
128614.text:
Consider the following sequence of physiological responses to excessive fluid loss from the body:

Excessive loss of fluid $\rightarrow$ activates [P] $\rightarrow$ stimulates hypothalamus $\rightarrow$ releases [Q] from neurohypophysis $\rightarrow$ causes [R] of blood vessels $\rightarrow$ leads to [S] in glomerular blood flow and GFR.

Identify [P], [Q], [R], and [S] correctly.
128614.sol:
Excessive fluid loss from the body activates osmoreceptors [P]. These receptors stimulate the hypothalamus to release Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) or vasopressin [Q] from the neurohypophysis. ADH exerts a constrictory effect (vasoconstriction) [R] on blood vessels, which raises blood pressure. This increase in blood pressure leads to an increase [S] in glomerular blood flow and Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR).

Option 1 is incorrect because osmoreceptors, not chemoreceptors, sense fluid volume changes, and ADH causes constriction, not dilation.
Option 2 is incorrect because ANF is released from the atria of the heart, not the neurohypophysis, and it causes vasodilation.
Option 4 is incorrect because ADH increases, rather than decreases, GFR by raising blood pressure.

Answer: [P] Osmoreceptors, [Q] ADH, [R] Constriction, [S] Increase

129233.text: What is the hindbrain responsible for?

129233.sol: The brain acts as the "command and control system" and controls various functions such as voluntary movements, balance, vital organs, circadian rhythms, endocrine glands and human behavior. The brain is divided into three major parts, the forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain, which are the main regions that control different functions in the body.The cranial meninges consisting of dura mater, arachnoid and pia mater protect the brain and act as a protective layer. The cranial meninges consist of three layers: dura mater, arachnoid and pia mater. The outer layer of the cranial meninges is called the dura mater. 129512.subject: Zoology
129512.text: What is not filtered by the glomerulus?
129512.sol: The first step in urine formation is the filtration of blood, which is carried out by the glomerulus and is called glomerular filtration. On an average, 1100-1200 ml of blood is filtered by the kidneys per minute which constitute roughly 1/5th of the blood pumped out by each ventricle of the heart in a minute. The glomerular capillary blood pressure causes filtration of blood through 3 layers, i.e., the endothelium of glomerular blood vessels, the epithelium of Bowman’s capsule and a basement membrane between these two layers. The epithelial cells of Bowman’s capsule called podocytes are arranged in an intricate manner so as to leave some minute spaces called filtration slits or slit pores. Blood is filtered so finely through these membranes, that almost all the constituents of the plasma except the proteins pass onto the lumen of the Bowman’s capsule. Therefore, it is considered as a process of ultra filtration.
129512.meta: What is not filtered by the glomerulus?

129520.subject: Zoology
129520.text: What is the main function of Juxta Glomerular Apparatus (JGA)?
129520.sol: The amount of the filtrate formed by the kidneys per minute is called glomerular filtration rate (GFR). GFR in a healthy individual is approximately 125 ml/minute, i.e., 180 litres per day ! The kidneys have built-in mechanisms for the regulation of glomerular filtration rate. One such efficient mechanism is carried out by juxta glomerular apparatus (JGA). JGA is a special sensitive region formed by cellular modifications in the distal convoluted tubule and the afferent arteriole at the location of their contact. A fall in GFR can activate the JG cells to release renin which can stimulate the glomerular blood flow and thereby the GFR back to normal.
